title: CelluWeave C: Added cellulose and swelling tradeoffs
mainFindings: The hydrogel exhibited a mean compressive modulus of 51.0 kPa.
The water uptake of the hydrogel was 12.5 g/g.
The reported mean compressive modulus of 51.0 kPa is 9.0 kPa higher than the P17 reported mean of 42.0 kPa.
Water uptake increased from 10.0 to 12.5 g/g relative to P17.
methods: Curing in 50 mmol/L calcium chloride for 10 minutes
methodsSummary: A nonliving hydrogel containing 2.0% w/v alginate and 1.2% w/v cellulose was cured in 50 mmol/L calcium chloride for 10 minutes, equilibrated for 24 hours, and subjected to wet compression at 10% strain.

limitations: One of six sheets exhibited visible brittle cracking during handling
The study did not establish a crack-rate confidence interval
No living-cell or safety testing occurred
